question: A motorcyclist safety barrier is a flexible band of malleable material that can be added to a guard rail as a third section at the bottom. Its purpose is to catch motorcyclists who have come off their vehicle in an accident, considerably reducing the risk of them having anything severed by the metal guard rail.

According to data on accidents in Italy, because of the absence of such a device, motorcycle deaths now account for 24.1 % of all road accident deaths, despite the fact that motorcyclists themselves only make up 13.4 % of traffic.

At EU level, guard rails are governed by the European Committee for Standardization (CEN) under Technical Specification 1317-8, which is a non-binding technical provision providing for assessments on the basis of which Member States can certify auxiliary devices for the protection of motorcyclists.

Does the Commission have data on the number of deaths and accidents caused by amputation due to the absence of a motorcyclist safety barrier in Europe? Will it put forward a legislative proposal to make the installation of this device mandatory?
answer: Directive 2008/96/EC (1) on road infrastructure safety management mandates that Member States evaluate and enhance the safety of their road networks, prioritising the most hazardous sections. This evaluation is based on two sets of data: crash records for each section and the physical features of the roads.

Although no specific technologies or technical specifications are mandated, accident-prone areas must be addressed, with special attention to vulnerable road users. The training of road safety auditors and all procedures for assessing road projects or existing infrastructure must consider the needs of vulnerable road users, including motorcyclists.

The Commission is developing guidance on the quality and safety of infrastructure for vulnerable road users and guidance for forgiving roadsides. These guidelines will address the safety risks posed by inappropriate road features to motorcyclists. Currently, the Commission does not possess specific data on motorcyclist fatalities due to the absence of safety barriers.

The Commission does not collect data on deaths and accidents caused specifically by the absence of motorcyclist safety barriers in Europe. CARE (2), a Community database, provides data on all road crashes resulting in death or injury in the EU Member States and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries.

It contains data on drivers and passengers, in motorised vehicles and on bicycles, as well as pedestrians involved in road crashes. Data are collected by the EU Member States from police and hospital sources.
